rules.notes: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS), art. 25 § 1. Read directly on 2026-09-03 on eur-lex.europa.eu (consolidated version). This is a European REGULATION, directly applicable in all member states WITHOUT national transposition (unlike a directive) — the same legal basis therefore applies, verbatim and without national variation, to Germany, Italy, Poland, and Spain (see their own quote.send below and in it.json/pl.json/es.json). A quote is not an invoice (see invoice.send further below, based on German tax law specific to the invoice): it is this general regime of non-discrimination of electronic writing, not a VAT text, that grounds sending a quote electronically — same architecture as fr.json's own quote.send (code civil art. 1366, a general text on evidence, not a tax text).

rules.notes: REUSES the citation already read by correction-routes/data/de.json (route CORRECTIVE_INVOICE, required) — § 31 Abs. 5 UStDV; UStAE 14.11 Abs. 1 S. 2, 4, 5, 11 and Abs. 2 S. 1, checked on 2026-08-29 (date preserved as-is: this text was not re-verified by THIS task, only reused where it settles exactly the same fact). This text settles exactly the question asked here: a German invoice already issued is NEVER corrected by rewriting it — the correction is made through a SEPARATE DOCUMENT that specifically refers to it (and does not even need its own invoice number) — never through a new draft save on the same document. The `statuses: ["draft"]` field applies this principle by refusing to re-save as a draft an invoice already 'sent' — same mechanics as fr.json's own invoice.save-draft (CGI art. 289 I.5) and pl.json/it.json/es.json/mx.json below, each sourced to its own national text but settling the SAME fact: the immutability of the ISSUED invoice.

provenance.sourceText: Eine Rechnung kann als elektronische Rechnung oder vorbehaltlich des Absatzes 2 als sonstige Rechnung übermittelt werden. [...] Die Übermittlung einer elektronischen Rechnung oder einer sonstigen Rechnung in einem elektronischen Format bedarf der Zustimmung des Empfängers, soweit keine Verpflichtung nach Absatz 2 Satz 2 Nummer 1 besteht.

rules.notes: § 14 Abs. 1 Satz 2 and Satz 5 UStG. Read directly on 2026-09-03 on gesetze-im-internet.de (the official portal of the federal Ministry of Justice, consolidated text) — reconfirmed by a second, independent reading of the entirety of Absatz 1 the same day. This text explicitly authorizes the ELECTRONIC transmission of a German invoice, exactly the equivalent of section VI of art. 289 CGI for France. NUANCE NOT MODELED HERE, to be aware of (same limitation as fr.json's own invoice.send): Satz 5 conditions electronic transmission on the RECIPIENT'S CONSENT, except where a structured electronic invoicing obligation already applies (Absatz 2 Satz 2 Nummer 1 — the German B2B mandate for structured electronic invoicing, being rolled out since 2025-01-01, Wachstumschancengesetz); this rule verifies neither that consent nor the applicability of the mandate, it only authorizes the ACT of sending within the tool. What would settle the exact timetable and thresholds of the structured mandate: follow the Wachstumschancengesetz and the implementing BMF-Schreiben — out of scope for this rule, which covers only the general admissibility of electronic sending.

Germany carries no active channel mandate today (transports/channel-policy/data/ ships only FR/IT), so this rule, unlike FR's own, is a plain unblock with no further branching for the acting mechanism to decide at runtime (actions/invoice-actions.ts's "validate" handler, issue #581) - a German invoice is always just numbered and locked, never routed to a real send, by this action. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS: the same research § 14 UStG's own structured-mandate timetable (Wachstumschancengesetz) would need once that mandate activates - see invoice.send's own notes above.

The tax question (UStG § 14 et seq.) bears on the ISSUED INVOICE that will result, not on this initial draft. To be confirmed by a dedicated review if a specific rule were ever to attach to the automated creation of invoice drafts.

The resulting balance is a PROJECTION displayed on screen, never a document status — see invoice.descriptor.ts.

EN 16931 is a European TECHNICAL STANDARD (directive 2014/55/EU) — this is not in itself a German legal obligation for THIS company to produce it. The format actually mandated nationally in Germany (XRechnung/ZUGFeRD, under the B2B mandate being rolled out since 2025-01-01 — see the invoice.send note above) is a DISTINCT subject (imposed channel/format), out of scope for this rule which only builds the voluntary standardized FORMAT, same distinction as fr.json/us.json for the same action. This rule therefore authorizes the voluntary DOWNLOAD of an EN 16931 export (a product convenience) without asserting that it is legally required IN THIS PRECISE FORM. What would settle the structured mandate itself: follow the Wachstumschancengesetz and the implementing BMF-Schreiben.

Exporting an invoice to an accounting tool is a product convenience; no specific text identified that would govern the very fact of offering this export. This action has in any case no registered implementation to date (see invoice-actions.ts) — the actual blocking comes from the 501, not from this rule.

Generating a public, unauthenticated link to an invoice's PDF is a product convenience of the same order as 'download-xml' just above: no text identified imposes or prohibits specifically the sharing of a link to an invoice already communicated to its legitimate recipient. Link security is a technical guarantee documented in share-links/share-links.service.ts, not a distinct legal requirement to source here. To be confirmed by a dedicated review if the structured B2B mandate (see invoice.send above) were ever to specifically govern this mode of making available.

rules.notes: REUSES the citation already read by correction-routes/data/de.json (route CREDIT_NOTE, allowed) — UStAE 14.11 Abs. 4 S. 1; UStAE 17.1 Abs. 3a S. 4-5, checked on 2026-08-29 (date preserved: reused, not re-verified by this task). Unlike fr.json/us.json (which leave credit-note.send unverified, judging that the tool's SEND — an internal status change, without transmission — is not in itself the legal act of issuing a credit note), this rule is here promoted to 'legal' because the precise fact needed — France/the US did not yet have a citation specific to the credit note at the time fr.json/us.json were written, Germany has one via correction-routes — is EXACTLY the one this citation settles: issuing a document that reduces the amount of a German invoice (a credit note/Gutschrift in the broad sense, NOT the self-billing Gutschrift of § 14 Abs. 2 Satz 6, which is a distinct mechanism) is an open OPTION, never a general obligation, except for the narrow case of § 17 Abs. 4 UStG (allocation of consideration across transactions at different rates) which this product mechanism does not model.

rules.notes: Issue #472. § 31 Abs. 5 UStDV, read verbatim on gesetze-im-internet.de (ustdv_1980/__31.html) on 2026-09-27. Read with § 14 Abs. 1 Satz 3 UStG, read on the same page set the same day: « Eine elektronische Rechnung ist eine Rechnung, die in einem strukturierten elektronischen Format ausgestellt, übermittelt und empfangen wird und eine elektronische Verarbeitung ermöglicht. » A correcting document takes the same FORM as the invoice it corrects, so where the invoice is a structured e-invoice the correction is one too. NO DISTINCT GERMAN DOCUMENT TYPE IS NEEDED BEYOND EN 16931's own: the KoSIT XRechnung delta this repository vendors (formats/vendored/de/XRechnung-UBL-validation-preprocessed.sch, itplr-kosit/xrechnung-schematron v2.5.0) lists the credit note among the codes BT-3 may carry, rule BR-DE-17: « 326 (Partial invoice), 380 (Commercial invoice), 384 (Corrected invoice), 389 (Self-billed invoice) und 381 (Credit note) [...] », and the credit-note export passes that delta with 0 error (formats/credit-note-formats.spec.ts). TERMINOLOGY TRAP, same page: the German « Gutschrift » of § 14 Abs. 2 Satz 5 UStG is a document issued by the RECIPIENT of the supply (self-billing, UNTDID 389), not a seller's credit note; this action never emits 389, and nothing in this product should translate this document type as « Gutschrift » in a tax sense. Whether a German credit note needs a number of its own stays the open question this file's own credit-note `numbering` fact records - unchanged by this rule.

resetProvenance.sourceText: (10) ¹Durch die fortlaufende Nummer (Rechnungsnummer) soll sichergestellt werden, dass die vom Unternehmer erstellte Rechnung einmalig ist. [...] ⁴Eine lückenlose Abfolge der ausgestellten Rechnungsnummern ist nicht zwingend. (11) ¹Bei der Erstellung der Rechnungsnummer bleibt es dem Rechnungsaussteller überlassen, wie viele und welche separaten Nummernkreise geschaffen werden, in denen eine Rechnungsnummer jeweils einmalig vergeben wird. ²Dabei sind Nummernkreise für zeitlich, geographisch oder organisatorisch abgegrenzte Bereiche zulässig, z. B. für Zeiträume (Monate, Wochen, Tage) [...] ⁴Es muss jedoch gewährleistet sein [...], dass die jeweilige Rechnung leicht und eindeutig dem jeweiligen Nummernkreis zugeordnet werden kann und die Rechnungsnummer einmalig ist.

formats.notes: UStAE 14.5 Abs. (10)-(11), read first-hand from the BMF's own current consolidated PDF (bundesfinanzministerium.de, "Umsatzsteuer-Anwendungserlass-aktuell.pdf", header "BMF-Schreiben vom 9. April 2026 - III C 3 - S 7157-a/00005/001/052", extracted with pdftotext) on 2026-09-28. Abs. 11 lets the issuer define its own Nummernkreise for "zeitlich [...] abgegrenzte Bereiche" (temporally delimited ranges) - the stated examples are months, weeks and days ("z. B.", non-exhaustive), but a calendar YEAR is the same kind of temporally delimited range, conditioned only on unambiguous assignment to the right range and uniqueness of the resulting number (sentence 4) - exactly what a {year}-{number} pattern guarantees. Abs. 10 sentence 4 additionally confirms no gapless sequence is required, which a fresh per-year counter does not provide either. NOT READ as an official-text sentence (secondary commentary only, Haufe): the specific worked example "2016001...2016750; erste Rechnung 2017 = 2017001" some secondary sources attribute to this provision.

Kept `unverified` rather than `legal` for that reason: this is one inference away from a text actually read about the credit note itself. What would settle it: UStAE 17.1 (Gutschrift/kaufmännische Rechnungskorrektur), read first-hand, on whether it says anything of its own about numbering.

provenance.resolutionNote: This scheme's `appliesTo: 'COMPANY'` value was originally set with no UStG text read at all (see this scheme's own git history). This task read §14 Abs. 4 UStG and §14a UStG directly at gesetze-im-internet.de (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__14.html and .../__14a.html, fetched 2026-09-01) and can now quote the exact provisions: § 14 Abs. 4 Satz 1 Nr. 2 UStG — 'Eine Rechnung muss folgende Angaben enthalten: ... 2. die dem leistenden Unternehmer vom Finanzamt erteilte Steuernummer oder die ihm vom Bundeszentralamt für Steuern erteilte Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer'. § 14a Abs. 3 Satz 2 UStG (innergemeinschaftliche Lieferung) — 'In der Rechnung sind auch die Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer des Unternehmers und die des Leistungsempfängers anzugeben.' § 14a Abs. 1 Satz 3 UStG (grenzüberschreitende sonstige Leistung nach § 3a Abs. 2 mit Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers im Ausland) states the identical sentence for that other cross-border case. `appliesTo` was changed from 'COMPANY' back to 'BOTH' (matching the removed compliance engine's own choice at git tag avant-refonte-documents, backend/src/compliance/profiles/data/de.ts) because § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 2 binds 'der leistende Unternehmer' — any business person issuing an invoice, whether organized as a company or as an individual registered/unregistered trader (Einzelunternehmer) — not companies specifically; German law does not gate this on legal form. `required` stays false for TWO independently sourced reasons, not one: (1) § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 2 itself offers Steuernummer OR Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer — either satisfies the law, so a USt-IdNr specifically is never itself a flat mandate, and this catalog has no separate 'Steuernummer' scheme (schema.ts's own header: 'LEGAL_ID' and 'VAT' are the only two schemes any shipped file uses today, a third would render with no dedicated data-cy) so a Steuernummer-holding, USt-IdNr-less business cannot be told apart from one that has neither; (2) § 14a's dual-VAT-number rule only fires for specific cross-border scenarios (intra-Community supply, or a cross-border B2B service under reverse charge), not every invoice, and a private consumer or a Kleinunternehmer (§19 UStG small-business exemption) has no USt-IdNr to give at all — the exact same 'no per-company VAT-regime input to condition on' reasoning `data/fr.json`'s own VAT entry in this same catalog already gives. What remains genuinely unsourced is the `pattern` itself: the DE + 9-digit format (ISO 7064 Mod 11,10 checksum) is well documented (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VAT_identification_number#Germany, cross-checked against this codebase's own `documents/tax/vat-syntax.ts#validateDeVat`, which cites the same Wikipedia page) but neither §14 nor §14a UStG states a format, and an attempt today (2026-09-01) to reach the issuing authority's own page (https://www.bzst.de/DE/Unternehmen/Identifikationsnummern/Umsatzsteuer_Identifikationsnummer/umsatzsteuer_identifikationsnummer_node.html) returned HTTP 404. Since schema.ts's own header treats `pattern` as a legal CLAIM covered by this fact's provenance exactly like `required`, and the pattern is the one piece not sourced to a primary/official text, the whole fact stays 'unverified' rather than being split — same all-or-nothing grading US EIN's entry in data/us.json already uses when a read text settles most, but not all, of a fact's claim. What would settle the pattern specifically: a BZSt or EU publication describing the USt-IdNr format directly.

This scheme did not exist in the shipped file before (only inherited as a candidate from the removed compliance engine's own DE profile, git tag avant-refonte-documents, backend/src/compliance/profiles/data/de.ts's requiredIdentifiers: scheme LEGAL_ID, label Handelsregisternummer, appliesTo COMPANY, no pattern — that profile carried NO provenance field at all, so its choice was never sourced there either). This task read § 37a HGB directly at gesetze-im-internet.de (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/hgb/__37a.html, fetched 2026-09-01): 'Auf allen Geschäftsbriefen des Kaufmanns gleichviel welcher Form, die an einen bestimmten Empfänger gerichtet werden, müssen seine Firma, die Bezeichnung nach § 19 Abs. 1 Nr. 1, der Ort seiner Handelsniederlassung, das Registergericht und die Nummer, unter der die Firma in das Handelsregister eingetragen ist, angegeben werden.' (§ 37a Abs. 1 HGB). Two things this text does NOT settle: (1) it governs 'Geschäftsbriefe' (business letters/correspondence) addressed to a specific recipient — the word 'Rechnung' (invoice) never appears in § 37a HGB at all, so whether an invoice counts as a Geschäftsbrief for this purpose is an interpretive question this task did not chase down to a further primary source (case law or an official commentary would settle it — none was read); (2) § 37a HGB binds a 'Kaufmann' (a merchant registered in the Handelsregister — GmbH, AG, OHG, KG, eingetragener Kaufmann/e.K.), not every company: a company that never registered as a Kaufmann (e.g. a small GbR) has no Handelsregisternummer to give at all, which is the reasoning behind `required: false`. Corroborating evidence the number is NOT a tax-invoice-law requirement: § 14 Abs. 4 UStG's own exhaustive list of the ten mandatory invoice particulars (read in this same research pass, see this file's VAT entry above) does not mention a Handelsregisternummer anywhere. `appliesTo` stays 'COMPANY' as in the removed profile — an individual German Kaufmann (e.K.) could in principle also hold a Handelsregisternummer, but that nuance was not chased further here. What would settle this: case law or an official commentary establishing whether a Rechnung is a Geschäftsbrief under § 37a HGB, and whether an individually-registered Kaufmann (as opposed to a corporate form) should also carry this requirement in this catalog's `appliesTo`.

provenance.sourceText: C'EST la voie allemande. Applicable à une facture à laquelle manquent les mentions des § 14 Abs. 4 / § 14a, ou dont les mentions sont « unzutreffend ». Seuls les éléments manquants ou faux doivent être envoyés : « Die Berichtigung muss durch ein Dokument erfolgen, das SPEZIFISCH UND EINDEUTIG AUF DIE RECHNUNG BEZOGEN ist » et « EINE NEUE RECHNUNGSNUMMER FÜR DIESES DOKUMENT IST NICHT ERFORDERLICH ». FORMAT LOCK: correcting an electronic invoice must itself be electronic, in the same document type (UStAE 14.11 Abs. 1 S. 7-9, BMF-Schreiben 15/10/2025) — symmetric to the Polish lock in art. 106j ust. 4.

Source : UStAE 14c.1 Abs. 7 S. 1-2.

LA SURPRISE ALLEMANDE — un cas étroit, mais une vraie autorisation préalable. Applicable au « Unberechtigter Steuerausweis » (§ 14c Abs. 1 S. 3), également § 1 Abs. 1a et révocation de l'option § 9. Le montant dû « kann berichtigt werden, soweit die GEFÄHRDUNG DES STEUERAUFKOMMENS BESEITIGT worden ist », et « Die Berichtigung… ist beim FINANZAMT GESONDERT SCHRIFTLICH ZU BEANTRAGEN UND NACH DESSEN ZUSTIMMUNG… vorzunehmen ». Elle annule la TAXE, pas la facture — mais c'est bien une autorisation d'autorité qui conditionne le cycle de correction. Source : § 14c Abs. 2 S. 3-5 UStG ; UStAE 14c.1 Abs. 11.

rates.notes: UStG § 12 Abs. 1. provenance.sourceText: (3) Die Steuer ermäßigt sich auf 0 Prozent für die folgenden Umsätze: 1. die Lieferungen von Solarmodulen an den Betreiber einer Photovoltaikanlage, einschließlich der für den Betrieb einer Photovoltaikanlage wesentlichen Komponenten und der Speicher, die dazu dienen, den mit Solarmodulen erzeugten Strom zu speichern, wenn die Photovoltaikanlage auf oder in der Nähe von Privatwohnungen, Wohnungen sowie öffentlichen und anderen Gebäuden, die für dem Gemeinwohl dienende Tätigkeiten genutzt werden, installiert wird. rates.notes: UStG § 12 Abs. 3 Nr. 1 (Nr. 2 to 4, not reproduced here, extend the same 0% rate to the intra-Community acquisition, importation and installation of the same systems/storage units — the same rule repeated, not transcribed). Same direct reading, same URL, same date as de-standard above. THIS IS NOT AN EXEMPTION but a genuine ZERO RATE in the EN 16931 sense (category ZERO, not EXEMPT): this provision sits in § 12, titled « Steuersätze » (tax rates), worded exactly like the 19%/7% subsections (« Die Steuer ermäßigt sich auf … Prozent »), and NOT in § 4 UStG (« Steuerbefreiungen », the exemptions) — a taxable person selling under this regime still invoices VAT (at 0%) and keeps full input-VAT deduction rights, which is the EN 16931 zero-rate behavior, not that of an exemption. This conclusion rests on the structure and title of § 12 itself (read directly above); the text of § 4 UStG was NOT independently read to contrast the wording in this research. NARROW scope: limited to solar modules and associated equipment for a photovoltaic installation installed on or near homes/buildings serving the public interest, with an installed gross capacity (Marktstammdatenregister) not exceeding 30 kilowatts-peak — not a general zero rate. Effective date (understood as 2023-01-01, via the Jahressteuergesetz 2022) NOT independently verified in this research: § 28 UStG, which is where the UStG's own transitional rules live, is silent on Abs. 3 — its effective date lives in the enacting law itself, not read here.

vatRates.notes: Germany (2026-09-13). Three rates, all 'legal', SOURCED FROM THE PRIMARY LEGAL TEXT as served by the Bundesministerium der Justiz on gesetze-im-internet.de (an unofficial but continuously regenerated consolidated text), direct curl + HTML parsing, never a fetch-summary: UStG § 12 Abs. 1 — 19% (Regelsteuersatz), Abs. 2 — 7% (ermäßigter Steuersatz), Abs. 3 Nr. 1 — 0% (Nullsteuersatz, residential/public-interest-building photovoltaics, narrow scope detailed on the de-zero-pv entry). NO SUPER_REDUCED TIER exists for Germany (only these two ordinary tiers plus the narrow zero rate) — do not invent one. A CAVEAT ON THE LABELS: unlike France (where « taux normal » appears literally in CGI art. 278) or Portugal (« taxa normal »/« taxa reduzida » on the AT's own page), the UStG NEVER NAMES its own rates in § 12 — it only gives numbers (« ermäßigt sich auf sieben Prozent », « ermäßigt sich auf 0 Prozent »). « Regelsteuersatz » / « ermäßigter Steuersatz » / « Nullsteuersatz » are the usual administrative/doctrinal terms (BMF, UStAE) and not words quoted from § 12 itself — this `label` field therefore carries a convention, not a literal official term from the statutory text (verified by confirming that none of these labels appears in the citations themselves above). This catalog still does not model the temporality of rates (no validFrom/validTo in schema.ts): only the rates CURRENTLY in force are listed. No EXEMPT entry is added for Germany: the small-business regime (Kleinunternehmerregelung, § 19 UStG) was not read at its primary text by this research and is therefore not encoded here, following the same discipline as the rest of this file.

channelPolicy.notes:
NO TRANSMISSION CHANNEL is imposed by German law for B2B invoicing — German law imposes a FORMAT, never a channel, unlike France (PDP) or Italy (SdI). Established by direct reading of the consolidated text of the UStG (Umsatzsteuergesetz) on gesetze-im-internet.de (official site of the Bundesministerium der Justiz), §§ 14 and 27, checked on 2026-09-13 (direct curl, no anti-bot block encountered).

§ 14 Abs. 1 UStG distinguishes two notions, never a channel: « Eine elektronische Rechnung ist eine Rechnung, die in einem strukturierten elektronischen Format ausgestellt, übermittelt und empfangen wird und eine elektronische Verarbeitung ermöglicht. Eine sonstige Rechnung ist eine Rechnung, die in einem anderen elektronischen Format oder auf Papier übermittelt wird. Die Übermittlung einer elektronischen Rechnung oder einer sonstigen Rechnung in einem elektronischen Format bedarf der Zustimmung des Empfängers, soweit keine Verpflichtung nach Absatz 2 Satz 2 Nummer 1 besteht. » — translation: an electronic invoice is an invoice issued, transmitted AND received in a structured electronic format enabling automated processing; any other invoice (another electronic format, or paper) is a « sonstige Rechnung ». The last sentence quoted conditions the recipient's consent to the transmission, never a channel: no word in this paragraph names a platform, a network, or an intermediary.

The obligation itself (Abs. 2) concerns only the FORMAT, never the channel: « Führt der Unternehmer eine Lieferung oder eine sonstige Leistung nach § 1 Absatz 1 Nummer 1 aus, ist er berechtigt, eine Rechnung auszustellen. In den folgenden Fällen ist er zur Ausstellung einer Rechnung innerhalb von sechs Monaten nach Ausführung der Leistung verpflichtet, wenn der Umsatz nicht nach § 4 Nummer 8 bis 29 steuerfrei ist: » then, at point 1 of that list (Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 1, the domestic B2B case): « für eine Leistung an einen anderen Unternehmer für dessen Unternehmen; die Rechnung ist als elektronische Rechnung nach Absatz 1 Satz 3 und 6 auszustellen, wenn der leistende Unternehmer und der Leistungsempfänger im Inland oder in einem der in § 1 Absatz 3 bezeichneten Gebiete ansässig sind; » — translation: for a supply to another business for that business's own use, the invoice MUST be issued as an electronic invoice (structured format defined in Abs. 1) when both the supplier AND the recipient are established in Germany (or in the assimilated territories of art. 1 Abs. 3). That is the entirety of the German B2B obligation: a structured format (XRechnung, or a ZUGFeRD-type hybrid compliant with the EN 16931 standard), never a channel — the business remains free to send that file by e-mail, by upload to a private portal, by direct EDI, or by any other means: nothing in this text names, or imposes, a transmission intermediary.

This format obligation is not immediately enforceable against all businesses: the transitional regime of § 27 Abs. 38 UStG (same consolidated text, same reading) postpones its effective application — « Abweichend von § 14 Absatz 1 und 2 kann eine Rechnung » then, in three points: « 1. bis zum 31. Dezember 2026 für einen nach dem 31. Dezember 2024 und vor dem 1. Januar 2027 ausgeführten Umsatz auf Papier oder vorbehaltlich der Zustimmung des Empfängers in einem elektronischen Format, das nicht § 14 Absatz 1 Satz 6 entspricht, übermittelt werden; », « 2. bis zum 31. Dezember 2027 für einen nach dem 31. Dezember 2026 und vor dem 1. Januar 2028 ausgeführten Umsatz auf Papier oder vorbehaltlich der Zustimmung des Empfängers in einem elektronischen Format, das nicht § 14 Absatz 1 Satz 6 entspricht, übermittelt werden, wenn der Gesamtumsatz (§ 19 Absatz 2) des die Rechnung ausstellenden Unternehmers im vorangegangenen Kalenderjahr nicht mehr als 800 000 Euro betragen hat; », « 3. bis zum 31. Dezember 2027 für einen nach dem 31. Dezember 2026 und vor dem 1. Januar 2028 ausgeführten Umsatz vorbehaltlich der Zustimmung des Empfängers in einem elektronischen Format, das nicht § 14 Absatz 1 Satz 6 entspricht, ausgestellt werden, wenn diese mittels elektronischem Datenaustausch (EDI) nach Artikel 2 der Empfehlung 94/820/EG der Kommission vom 19. Oktober 1994 über die rechtlichen Aspekte des elektronischen Datenaustausches (ABl. L 338 vom 28.12.1994, S. 98) übermittelt wird. » — in plain terms: (1) ANY business may still issue on paper or in an unstructured electronic format (PDF included), with the recipient's agreement, for any transaction carried out up to and including 31 December 2026, with no turnover condition at all; (2) businesses whose total turnover (§ 19 Abs. 2) for the preceding calendar year did not exceed €800,000 keep this same freedom for one more year, until 31 December 2027, for transactions carried out in 2027; (3) any business transmitting via electronic data interchange (EDI) also keeps this freedom until 31 December 2027 for 2027 transactions, regardless of its turnover. It is therefore only from 1 January 2028 that the structured-format obligation applies, with no transitional exception left, to every business covered by Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 1.

WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT ENCODE, AND WHY: `mandate.ts#activeChannelMandateFor` only knows a pair (providerId, mandatedFrom) — one channel and a single date. German law supplies neither in the sense this mechanism expects them: (a) there is structurally NO channel to name — even once the format obligation is fully in force on 1 January 2028, the law still only requires a format, never a drop-off point; inventing a `providerId` here ("email", "peppol" or otherwise) would assert a channel requirement the text never makes; (b) even granting, mistakenly, that this file should cover a FORMAT obligation rather than a channel one, a single date would not be enough to represent the two-speed timetable (universal until 31/12/2026, businesses ≤ €800,000 or EDI users until 31/12/2027, everyone from 1 January 2028) without knowing each company's prior-year (N-1) turnover or whether it uses EDI — two pieces of data this product neither computes nor stores today. This file therefore stays at `facts: []`: neither `mandated` (there is no channel to mandate) nor `suggested` (no source lets us claim any particular channel is "the custom" — unlike Poland, where the text explicitly names KSeF as THE legal system, even though it is not yet armed today for similar threshold reasons).

WHAT IS ALREADY COVERED ELSEWHERE, DELIBERATELY NOT REPEATED HERE: German B2G (invoices to federal public buyers, a separate obligation grounded in the ERechV rather than the UStG) does impose a channel — the merged ZRE/OZG-RE federal platform — fully sourced in `b2g-routing/data/de.json`, whose `transportId` names this channel (`zre-ozgre`) even though no transport in this repository implements it today: between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-15 this repository wired and proved in real conditions an access route via Peppol (accepted by the merged platform as a channel, carrying XRechnung content), but this transport was removed from the product on 2026-09-15 (see the dated ADDENDUM in `b2g-routing/data/de.json`'s own `notes` for the reason and what it would take to restore it) — a German B2G send therefore now returns a named refusal rather than a real send. This file (`channel-policy`) covers only the general B2B question; it is neither contradicted by, nor a duplicate of, that B2G rule.

WHAT THIS READING DID NOT ESTABLISH, HONESTLY: (1) a possible separate, non-transitional RECEPTION obligation (being able to receive a structured electronic invoice from 1 January 2025, independently of the issuance tolerance in Abs. 38) was not specifically researched beyond what the last sentence of Abs. 1 quoted above suggests (the recipient's consent is no longer required once an Abs. 2 Satz 2 Nr. 1 obligation exists) — this nuance changes nothing about the conclusion "no channel", so it was not dug into further; (2) the scope of Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 1 is strictly domestic (supplier AND recipient both established in Germany) — cross-border transactions from Germany fall under other provisions (§ 14 Abs. 7, § 14a) not read here in detail; this reading therefore does not cover them.

rules.label: umsatzsteuerlich
rules.notes: Raw text retrieved on 2026-09-13 via curl -A "Mozilla/5.0" https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__14b.html (HTTP 200). Satz 1: « Der Unternehmer hat ein Doppel der Rechnung, die er selbst oder ein Dritter in seinem Namen und für seine Rechnung ausgestellt hat, sowie alle Rechnungen, die er erhalten oder die ein Leistungsempfänger oder in dessen Namen und für dessen Rechnung ein Dritter ausgestellt hat, acht Jahre aufzubewahren. » — EIGHT years, not ten (the reduction from ten to eight years is in force; do not "correct" it back to the old ten-year duration some older sources still cite). Satz 3, the origin: « Die Aufbewahrungsfrist beginnt mit dem Schluss des Kalenderjahres, in dem die Rechnung ausgestellt worden ist; § 147 Abs. 3 der Abgabenordnung bleibt unberührt. » — the end of the CALENDAR year of issuance, never the moment of archiving. The last clause (« § 147 Abs. 3 ... bleibt unberührt » = "remains unaffected") is the text itself stating that the Abgabenordnung's own obligation (see the "abgabenrechtlich" rule below) applies IN ADDITION, not instead — the same simultaneity compute-retention.ts already documents for France.

rules.label: abgabenrechtlich
rules.legalRef: AO § 147 Abs. 3 Satz 1 (facture = Buchungsbeleg, Abs. 1 Nr. 4), Abs. 4
rules.notes: Raw text retrieved on 2026-09-13 via curl -A "Mozilla/5.0" https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__147.html (HTTP 200). Abs. 1 lists the categories: Nr. 1 (books/inventories/annual accounts...), Nr. 2/3 (Handels- oder Geschäftsbriefe received/sent — general business correspondence), Nr. 4 (Buchungsbelege — accounting vouchers), Nr. 4a (customs documents), Nr. 5 (other records relevant for taxation). Abs. 3 Satz 1: « Die in Absatz 1 Nummer 1 und 4a aufgeführten Unterlagen sind zehn Jahre, die in Absatz 1 Nummer 4 aufgeführten Unterlagen acht Jahre und die sonstigen in Absatz 1 aufgeführten Unterlagen sechs Jahre aufzubewahren... » — an invoice is an ACCOUNTING VOUCHER (Buchungsbeleg, Nr. 4: it documents a transaction and underlies a ledger entry), not a mere business letter (Nr. 2/3) nor a customs document (Nr. 4a): it therefore falls under the EIGHT-year tier, not ten — picking ten years because it is the largest number in the sentence would be exactly the mistake this module exists to avoid. Abs. 4, the origin: « Die Aufbewahrungsfrist beginnt mit dem Schluss des Kalenderjahrs, in dem ... der Buchungsbeleg entstanden ist... » — the end of the calendar year in which the accounting voucher was drawn up, so the same origin (end of the year of issuance) as the UStG rule above. The two rules above yield the SAME duration (8 years) via two distinct texts that the text itself declares simultaneous (« § 147 Abs. 3 ... bleibt unberührt » in the UStG rule) — declared here as two separate rules rather than merged, to stay faithful to what each text actually says rather than assuming they will always coincide.

retention.notes: Two distinct texts (UStG § 14b and AO § 147) each impose EIGHT years from the end of the calendar year of issuance — see the per-rule notes above for the demonstration that an invoice does fall under the AO's eight-year tier (Buchungsbeleg, Abs. 1 Nr. 4) and not the ten-year tier (Nr. 1/4a, reserved for books/annual accounts/customs documents). Sources consulted as RAW TEXT on 2026-09-13: gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__14b.html and gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__147.html (both HTTP 200).

field.label: Supply type
field.helpText: Whether this line is a delivery of goods or a supply of services — it decides how a cross-border sale is taxed. Goods sold to a consumer in another EU member state are an intra-Community distance sale, taxed where they arrive once your EU-wide distance sales pass EUR 10 000 in a calendar year (Directive 2006/112/EC art. 33(a) and art. 59c); the same sale as a service stays taxable here (art. 45). Optional: a line that declares nothing is treated as a supply of services.

countryFields.notes: Germany's FIRST field-overlay file — same mechanism and shape as France's own `fr.json` (`lines[].supplyType`), applied here at the DOCUMENT level instead of a line: BT-10 ("Buyer reference") is a document-wide fact, not a per-line one. Added as an OPTIONAL top-level field (`path: ''` — schema.ts's own top-level convention) rather than a change to the trunk `invoice.descriptor.ts`: BT-10 only becomes MANDATORY under the XRechnung/Peppol deltas (`formats/xrechnung-provider.ts`'s BR-DE-15, `formats/peppol-bis-provider.ts`'s PEPPOL-EN16931-R003), never at the base EN 16931 layer every OTHER seller builds against — the same 'a country's own difference from the trunk is data, never a change forced on everyone' discipline `country-fields/schema.ts`'s own header documents. `formats/shared-build.ts#extractBuyerReference` reads `data.buyerReference` generically, off ANY document regardless of which overlay (if any) put an input for it on screen — see that function's own header: a seller in a country with no overlay for this field (e.g. a French seller invoicing a German public body, the exact case XRechnung exists for) has no SCREEN control for it today, a known, documented UX gap, not a format that refuses to serve them — the underlying JSON value, however it got there, is read the same way for every seller. Labeled directly (no i18n key), matching every other field label already shipped on `fr.json`'s own `supplyType` overlay and `invoice.descriptor.ts` itself — see that file's own comment on `DocumentFieldDescriptor.label` for why the frontend renders it verbatim, never through `t()`. SECOND OPERATION, added later: the SAME `supplyType` line subfield France's own `fr.json` already adds, byte-identical in key, kind, label, options and optionality — a LINE subfield, unlike `buyerReference` above. WHY THE FIELD IS IDENTICAL IN ALL FIVE COUNTRIES RATHER THAN A PER-COUNTRY VARIANT: what reads it — `tax/resolve-invoice-tax.ts`, feeding `tax/tax-engine.ts#determineLineTax` — branches on the goods/services distinction of Directive 2006/112/EC (arts. 32, 33(a) and 59c for an intra-Community distance sale of goods, art. 45 for a service), which binds every member state identically; the same reasoning `tax/types.ts`'s own `DistanceSalesRegime` states for art. 59c ('art. 59c applies identically in all of them'). Germany's transposition defines the two in the directive's own terms — « Lieferungen eines Unternehmers sind Leistungen, durch die er oder in seinem Auftrag ein Dritter den Abnehmer oder in dessen Auftrag einen Dritten befähigt, im eigenen Namen über einen Gegenstand zu verfügen (Verschaffung der Verfügungsmacht) » (UStG § 3 Abs. 1) against « Sonstige Leistungen sind Leistungen, die keine Lieferungen sind. Sie können auch in einem Unterlassen oder im Dulden einer Handlung oder eines Zustands bestehen » (UStG § 3 Abs. 9), the residual definition the directive itself uses. Read in raw text on 2026-09-21 at gesetze-im-internet.de (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__3.html). WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT MIRRORED FROM FRANCE: the French overlay's own `helpText` names BT-23 (« cadre de facturation »), which is a FRENCH obligation — `formats/semantic/business-process.ts#resolveFrenchBusinessProcessCode` derives that code only for a seller whose country has an active BT-23 rule in `content-requirements/`, and France is the only country with one — so a German seller declaring a supply type changes the exported document not at all; it changes the TAX determination, which is what this operation's own help text names instead. NO RETROACTIVE EFFECT ON STORED DOCUMENTS: the field is OPTIONAL and nothing back-fills it. `resolve-invoice-tax.ts` narrows a line's raw `supplyType` to GOODS/SERVICES and treats anything else — including absent — as SERVICES, emitting a named warning; that fallback is untouched here, so every invoice stored before this operation existed resolves exactly as it did before, and only a line a user explicitly marks as goods reaches the distance-sales branch. DIGITAL IS NOT OFFERED, on purpose: `tax/types.ts`'s own `SupplyType` has a third value, but `resolve-invoice-tax.ts` narrows a stored value to GOODS/SERVICES only, so a 'DIGITAL' option would be silently discarded on the way in — offering it would need that narrowing widened first, for all five countries including France.

b2gRouting.notes:
READ DIRECTLY on 2026-09-01 at gesetze-im-internet.de (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/erechv/__4.html and .../__5.html — verbatim citations above, extracted from the official German text itself). EUROPEAN BASELINE: directive 2014/55/EU, art. 7 (see fr.json's own note for the full citation — the same baseline applies to all three countries in this wave). DECISION ON THE TRANSPORT — SETTLED BY READING, NOT GUESSED: the text read (§ 4 Abs. 3 ERechV) explicitly REQUIRES a deposit via "ein Verwaltungsportal des Bundes" (a FEDERAL administrative portal within the meaning of the Onlinezugangsgesetz — the "OZG"), with prior registration via a "Nutzerkonto" — this is neither a plain e-mail send nor a channel already implemented in this repository (email/pdp/ksef/sdi). `transportId: "zre-ozgre"` therefore DELIBERATELY references the two federal platforms actually known under these names (ZRE — Zentrale Rechnungseingangsplattform des Bundes; OZG-RE — the shared OZG platform for the Länder that joined it), which do NOT EXIST in `transports/transport-registry.ts` — the exact same thesis as the French "chorus-pro" block (see fr.json's own note and actions/invoice-actions.ts's own header): sending an invoice by e-mail to a German federal public entity does NOT SATISFY the text above (which requires the PORTAL, not merely the XRechnung format), so silently routing to "email" would do exactly what this project refuses elsewhere (serve an artifact that LOOKS compliant — the right XML format — without going through the channel the law actually mandates). Sending therefore blocked, by naming it, until a ZRE/OZG-RE channel (or Peppol, if ever adopted as an alternative) was actually implemented — it was PEPPOL that was adopted and wired, see the ADDENDUM 2026-09-02 below for the full resolution. ASSUMED LIMITATION: the ERechV read here is the FEDERAL (Bund) text — each of Germany's 16 Länder has its own e-invoicing ordinance, potentially different (its own portal, or even a less strict channel); this rule covers ONLY what a uniform federal text allows asserting for the whole country, never an average or an assumption about the Länder — settling that would mean reading all 16 regional texts one by one, out of this task's scope. — ADDENDUM 2026-09-02 (wiring the 'peppol' transport — RESOLVED): READ DIRECTLY at https://www.e-rechnung-bund.de/faq/ (official site, operated by the Beschaffungsamt des BMI — the federal Ministry of the Interior's own procurement office): since September 2025, ZRE and OZG-RE have MERGED into a single platform (« Ein Jahr nach der Zusammenführung von ZRE und OZG-RE »), and this merged platform explicitly lists Peppol as ONE of its official deposit channels, alongside web entry, upload, and e-mail: « Die OZG-RE bietet als weiteren Übertragungskanal die Möglichkeit zum Rechnungsversand aus der erstellenden Software mittels Übertragung über das Peppol-Netzwerk an. » ("OZG-RE offers, as a further transmission channel, the possibility of sending an invoice from the issuing software via the Peppol network."). WHAT STILL BLOCKED AS OF THAT DATE: this repository's `peppol` transport (`transports/peppol-transport.ts`) built EXCLUSIVELY a generic Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 artifact (`formats/peppol-bis-provider.ts`), never an XRechnung one (`formats/xrechnung-provider.ts`) — yet § 4 Abs. 1 ERechV cited above explicitly requires XRechnung as the CONTENT, independent of which transmission channel is used; silently routing to `peppol` would have delivered generic Peppol-BIS content over a recognized-compliant channel, with no way for this repository to claim that content itself satisfies XRechnung. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS RULE: `transportId` reverts to `zre-ozgre` — exactly the value and reasoning of the original entry above, before the 2026-09-02 addendum. `formatSyntax` stays `xrechnung`: the CONTENT obligation (§ 4 Abs. 1 ERechV) is a fact of the world, unchanged by this removal; only the CHANNEL disappears. The `formatOverride` mechanism (`transport-registry.ts`'s own header) that carried the XRechnung build instead of Peppol BIS stays in place, dormant, for the day either of those exists.
